extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying to the Branco Weiss Fellowship (2027 intake)
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility, duration, and funding rules for applicants to the Branco Weiss Fellowship (2027 intake), including PhD timing, career stage restrictions, project originality expectations, leave-extension rules, project duration/phases, and permitted uses/amount of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD awarded / defended by cut-off date
rubrics_metrics.description: You officially hold a PhD on January 15, 2027. This means that you have at least successfully passed your PhD defense before January 15, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must have completed their PhD defense by the specified cut-off (Jan 15, 2027). The phrase 'officially hold a PhD' is defined as having at least successfully passed the defense by that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum time since PhD
rubrics_metrics.description: You have obtained your PhD a maximum of five years prior to January 15, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard eligibility window is 5 years post-PhD as of the intake cut-off; exceptions for documented full-time leave are possible (see 'acceptable delays' entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: No faculty-equivalent position held
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not hold/have not held a faculty-equivalent position (e.g. assistant professor or lecturer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must not have previously held positions equivalent to faculty appointments. Examples explicitly given include assistant professor or lecturer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project departs from mainstream research
rubrics_metrics.description: Your project departs from the mainstream of research in your discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation typically does not fund mainstream research projects that could also be funded by other scientific organizations. Projects should be original, unconventional, or pursue non-mainstream directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of outstanding scientific achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: You have a record of outstanding scientific achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to demonstrate exceptional scientific accomplishments in their track record; no specific metrics are listed on this page, but this is an explicit eligibility expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement beyond disciplinary frontiers
rubrics_metrics.description: You demonstrate in the proposal a willingness to engage in a dialog on relevant social, cultural, political or economic issues beyond the frontiers of your particular discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal should explicitly show willingness and intent to engage with broader societal issues beyond narrow disciplinary concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to attend annual symposium in person
rubrics_metrics.description: You can confirm that you are willing and able to travel to the Greater Zurich Area and attend the annual symposium in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical attendance at the annual symposium in the Greater Zurich Area is a stated expectation of fellows; applicants must confirm willingness and ability to travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor supports only one candidate per round
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ensure that you are the only candidate your chosen mentor is supporting during this round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mentor may support only one candidate in a given application round; applicants must confirm their chosen mentor is not supporting other candidates concurrently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-applicability for prior applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have applied before and were not selected, you are welcome to apply again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous non-selection does not bar re-application; candidates may submit again in subsequent intakes if other eligibility criteria are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable reasons for post-PhD delay (extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the following reasons for delays after attaining your PhD are acceptable: parental leave; inability to work due to illness or accident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking extension of the 5-year post-PhD window must provide official confirmation of these leaves. The Foundation accepts the number of weeks the research work was interrupted as an extension (max. 1 year in total). Only periods of full-time leave are taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and timing for leave-extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must send an official confirmation of their leave(s) via email to [email protected] before they submit an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is advisable to send such documents before starting your application and ideally 1–2 months before the annual deadline. Failure to provide timely official confirmation may affect eligibility for an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration: five-year design
rubrics_metrics.description: Research projects should be conceived to last five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects must be planned for a five-year period, aligning with the fellowship's structure (pioneer + exploitation phases). Budgeting and milestones should reflect a five-year timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project phases: pioneer and exploitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The first two and a half years of a project are called the pioneer phase; the remaining two and a half years are the exploitation phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the end of the second year a site visit and review will take place. If the evaluation and site visit are satisfactory, the fellow continues into the exploitation phase. Fellows are encouraged to seek faculty positions during the exploitation phase; starting a faculty position/professorship after the first year is permitted and will not result in termination of the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mid-term evaluation focus (site visit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the end of the second year a site visit will take place and a review will be conducted. At this point, the project, its continued originality, and the productivity of the fellow will be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation into the exploitation phase depends on satisfactory results of this review/site visit. Evaluators will assess whether the project remains original and whether the fellow's productivity merits continuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and permitted uses
rubrics_metrics.description: A Branco Weiss Fellowship amounts to max. CHF 600,000 for up to five years. It may be used to cover all legitimate costs of research (i.e. salary and/or equipment, travel expenses, consumables, personnel, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is provided up to the stated cap and may be allocated flexibly across typical research costs; applicants should plan budgets within this maximum and for a five-year duration.
